label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Bow summit summer trail/trees
reports.comment:
quick: Snow deep enough to set a good track up summer trail and around roadside tree area. Found a run with enough new and wind blown snow to get a few good turns in. Hit bottom a couple times but lower half was bouncy and soft keeping turns quick and shallow.
Recommend waiting until next significant snowfall passes if you want to be safer on the downhill. If your objective is a nice walk in the m…

reports.title: Happy Halloween
reports.comment:
quick: Skied 2 laps in the lower half of the Dogleg couloir (6 tracks total). 3 laps in the trees/chutes below.
Conditions were unreal for October, the last chute we skied seemed to be more uniformly supportive and skied like mid winter. / avalanche: From dogleg in the Dogleg couloir 2 x Skier controlled sz 0.5 loose-snow + slab down 20-30cm, width 1m. Broke into slough in less than a 1m

reports.title: Dog Leg Couloir + Bow Summit Trees
reports.comment: quick: Between 40-70cm of loose powder with little to no base in the trees depending on elevation.  Really good skiing for this time of year in the trees at higher elevations. Things are much patchier above treeline with some good skiing in sheltered areas but many sharks lurk beneath the surface, especially on wind-exposed features which are still very rocky. The snow in Dog Leg Couloir is much f…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Good early season conditions on mellow alpine slopes. Lots of traffic and harder to find fresh turns throughout the day. / snowpack: 70cm on mellow alpine slopes. <40cm on steeps with full pen to ground. 100cm+ on wind loaded.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Jimmy Jr had good early season conditions.  Snowpack depth ranged from 110cm to 5cm.  No signs of instability. Some very small sluffs off the south steep terrain as the day warmed. 
Some sharks lurking, but we only found them on the central moraines in the lower section of the bowl when going slow heading to transition and skin back up. Three parties out (one group of six included) pretty t…

reports.title: Bow summit / Jimmy Simpson Junior Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Skied slopes above treeline on lookers left then traversed into Jimmy Simpson Junior Bowl. Westward slopes were wind affected but the bowl collected enough transported snow to save the base of our skis. Snow was poorly consolidated in the bowl.

Not an issue today but the cold and clear weather has developed a layer of surface hoar just past the treeline.

reports.title: C-train approach,Crowfoot Mountain north end
reports.comment: quick: Approached the route Where the Sidewalk Ends on the north end of Crowfoot Mountain. Didn't find the climb but found 30-40 cms facets to ground on the approach slopes above Bow Lake. Windcrusts didn't generally impede or help foot travel, generally standing on the ground.  Roped up at the pinch point below C-train, but the slopes up and left to the Sidewalk area were unreactive.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak Wind Slab Avalanche
reports.comment: incident: Remote triggered a wind slab avalanche on the southwest aspect of Observation Sub Peak from above and one “gully” to skiers left. Propagated thin to thick and into immediate lee of wind lip that existed along the ridge, followed the wind lip down the ridge, and initiated a wind slab avalanche taking out most of the face sliding on facets to ground. Our party was investigating the face fo…

reports.title: Sidewalk Route North Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Climbed the first four pitches of the Sidewalk route.  Blowing all day, only felt ok with approach as trail was broken two days ago, with snow and wind in the forecast might not have headed there otherwise.

Snow blowing across Bow Lake was visible during the day. On descent new pockets of wind slab had only accumulated in a few spots, not as much as expected. Only trace new snow during the…

reports.title: Helens shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Triggered a small slab avalanche while approaching a rocky outcrop. Top of Crown to bottom of the deposit was approx. 30~50m.

Also had some shooting cracks on similar features and a few whumpfs on the transition to the flat of similar features.

Skiing was best at tree line on NE Asp. A thin breakable crust was present ~10cm down. On W,S and SE asp.

reports.title: Bow Summit Chutes and Skin Tracks
reports.comment:
weather: 1140hrs @2290m, obscured, S1, Temp High: -7 Low: -12, HN24 12cm, HS 90cm, Winds L-M N

(Winds started from the West, shifting to N throughout the day, snow consistent with periods of S-1 to S2.) / snowpack: No avalanche observations today, no signs of instability in the area we skied.

reports.title: Dolomite Traverse - Don't follow our tracks.
reports.comment: quick: Poor snow conditions on Dolomite traverse. "Whumphing" at multiple aspects and elevations above treeline. Shooting cracks, though on test slopes the slab seemed hard to budge (possibly due to compressive support from below, better test slopes were not easily accessible) . "Soft slab" below treeline but firmer / more wind affected at TL and above. Katherine Lake is not fully frozen, slushy a…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Surprised to find great coverage, 40+cm of fresh untracked snow. Some areas wind effected, but generally great snow. Fun day with warmer temps than anticipated.

reports.title: Nile
reports.comment: quick: Short trip up the in the Nile area. Week of very cold temps and little snow made for mediocre riding conditions. Rode East aspect. There was no wind, but observed the beginning of cornice formation overhead. Looking across the highway, major wind affected areas and loose dry snow. Experienced shooting cracks on our way up, no whumpfing or slides observed. Snow quality was great, just needs …

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: No new avalanche observations, 1 roughly 48+ hr old size 1 on a cross loaded alpine feature, unknown trigger but suspected remote trigger from an above skin track.  Quick pit at 2200m on low angle N aspect showed the presence of Nov 17th and Nov 22 interfaces both non-reactive in compression tests. Facets from top to bottom (~80cm) aside from the Nov 17 crust which seems to be breaking down…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades wind slab
reports.comment: quick: Triggered a small slab in Crowfoot Glades area, far away from main runs. An isolated wind loaded slab 15m long and 0.30m thick triggered by a snowboarder. The slab traveled slow behind the rider, stopped in concave below. Traveled on facets layer with soft snow below. Noone was caught. Touchy conditions outthere. Stay safe.

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson Hidden Bowl/Glades
reports.comment: quick: Early Season up Hidden Bowl, opted to set track through the trees lookers left of the bowl due to a group of 17 in the bowl at the time. We ended up lapping the slide paths on the East Aspect of Jimmy, overall ride quality was good, though it's almost 60-70cm snow with little to no support until the Nov 16 BF/SH/SC layer and then obviously facets to ground. We found some slab problems on th…

reports.title: signs of instability
reports.comment: quick: We had grand plans, but once we got up to the Bow summit area, we could see the wind was really cranking in the Alpine. We decided to keep it simple, and we were glad we did, as we had pretty much consistent whumpfing and shooting cracks on all alpine slopes. The slab on top of the November facets has stiffened up and made the possibility of triggering an avalanche much more likely. I would…

reports.title: Observation Trees
reports.comment: quick: Skied treeline and below treeline on Observation. Great snow conditions with deep powder everywhere. Some cracking and whumpfing observed but overall the snow felt stable. Skied on the border of treeline and alpine but stuck to long angle terrain. Lots of sharks still present!

reports.title: Bow Summit snowpack
reports.comment:
quick: 80 cm deep, weak snowpack at Bow Summit treeline. Buried crust and surface hoar in the middle of the snowpack with facets and depth hoar below. CT 11 taps fails Sudden Collapse just below the crust, then the depth hoar below crumbles away while trying to do tests.

Skiing was nice on the surface with 10 cm soft pow, but felt very tentative with all of the rocks around. Very careful skiing.

reports.title: Bow Peak Trees
reports.comment: quick: The snowpack was approximately 100 cm deep. Significant depth hoar throughout the bottom 70-ish centimeters. We didn't notice any whumping while skiing or any fracturing.  We skied in fairly dense trees all day, and didn't venture into the alpine as there was significant exposed rock.

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir Fan - Brrr
reports.comment: quick: Super cold day skiing the fan below the crowfoot couloir. -39° according to the car thermometer. Riding conditions were great with a mix of wind affected and soft powder. Worth it? Meh. Only could suffer 2 hours of it before heading into the car. Evidence of class 1 dry loose slides on all steep faces with long run-outs. I’d be careful skiing anything steep in the next bit. Sorry I couldn’t…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Skied a few laps in crowfoot glades. Snowed all day, maybe 5cm of new when we left. Great snow quality but still then. Tracked out in spots. Soft labs at tree line and quickly becoming wind slabs. A few shooting cracks and lots of sluff, things seemed to becoming more reactive by end of day.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Pretty tracked out from yesterday with only 5cm overnight was not enough to fill in tracks. Skiing was variable but mostly soft and ok. / avalanche: 1 sz 2 observed over extreme unskiable terrain. Prior to observing this we saw signs of 2 previous slides possibly triggered from previous activity off of unskiable terrain.

Audible of 2 more avalanches also in extreme unskiable terrain not vi…

reports.title: Boxing Day Jimmy Jr. Trees
reports.comment:
quick: Snowy day in the Jimmy Jr Trees today. 25 cm of recent storm snow over the Dec 17 layer, producing moderate to low-end results with stability tests. Snow depth of 120 cm. 

Unconsolidated deep facets made for a weaker snowpack and difficult uptracking.  

Saw a size 2 avalanche starting from above the lookers right of Jimmy Jr bowl, coming down into the ski line.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Nice day out in West Nile area. Snowfall intensified around noon. We estimated approx. 20 cm of fresh snow and 100-120 cm HS. Ski pen was up to 60 cm which made it for a good workout. The winds picked up at higher elevations. We heard a few slides from distance above treeline, so we turned around to keep it safe.

reports.title: Crowfoot Trees snow profile
reports.comment: quick: Minimal wind effect in Crowfoot Trees today, which is surprising considering it was blowing almost 100 km/hr at ridge crests. Sheltered by the big rock wall to the west.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skiing was really great, new snow on top of wind effected snow, variable a bit on the open SW slope but better lower down. Snow in the trees on the SE side of the ridge was much better. Trail breaking wasn’t much of issue, snow was mostly supportive even though the base is made up of facets. / snowpack: ECTN28

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Poor snowpack and not so great skiing. Beautiful trip out for scenery as you have views for most of the way.  We had an average snowpack depth of 80cm, of which the bottom 40-50cm was facets. There is a slab near the surface that is about 10-30cm thick but mostly non-supportive to skis. Felt whoomphing and cracking while skinning up.  The tails of our skis often sank on both the way up and …

reports.title: West Nile avalanche
reports.comment: incident: Group skinned up low angle terrain and waited beneath rocks on climber's right. First skier crossed a supportive compression which had already cracked on approach but not slid due to the low angle and supportive shape. Skier came back to wait in rocky terrain higher on climber's right where rocks seemed to break up the terrain too much for a continuous bed surface. Second skier followed …

reports.title: Mount Gordon (Wapta)
reports.comment: quick: Because of the forecast we chose to go for a long walk with lower angle objectives. I do this tour every year sometimes earlier in the season this is the lowest amount of snow I have seen. The approach slope to Bow Hut has just enough coverage to make it passable up and down no obvious signs of instability were observed on that. The Toe of the glacier skied the best, soft, light snow. Above…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: 5 cm H24 and 30 cm overtop of Dec 17 layer. CTH21, sudden collapse in facets below Nov 25 layer x 2. No results on Dec 17. Unconsolidated snowpack making for difficult trail breaking and skiing.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: We went up to Crowfoot Glades to gather information about the snowpack, riding mellow slopes and the creek gully down. Skin track up to Crowfoot Glades was well established. We saw no signs of recent avalanche activity. Dug a pit on N 28° in TL 2213m: CTE 6(SP), 5(SP) at 80cm on FC Dec 17, CTM 18(BRK), 14(BRK) at 30cm on DH/FC Nov 16. Some nice turns in TL but the gully/creek was tracked ou…

reports.title: Skier triggered persistent slab
reports.comment: quick: Sz 1.5 Skier triggered slab between Jimmy Junior and Bow Summit in the past 72 hrs.

reports.title: OXO/Puzzle Peak
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly decent skiing on OXO today. Snowpack at TL and above was relatively supportive with ski pen averaging 20cms, but up to 50 in, thinner areas lacking the supportive slab over the basal FC.  Evidence of an older natural avalanche cycle up to sz 2.5 in the ALP, suspect ran in the basal FC. Experienced some settlements and shooting cracks in shallow areas on but no movement on the l…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Quick lap at West Nile to TL. Facets to ground with no supportive layer. Some small surface hoar development up to 2100m where we turned around, but possibly higher as well. Evidence of a Na size 2 slab avalanche on the SE upper face of Bow Peak from the past day or two. Beautiful day out, good for a leg stretch.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Bizarre skiing conditions, bottomless facets with poor floatation at treeline and below. Very difficult trailbreaking below treeline, improving in the alpine but thin coverage. Lots of rocks in the alpine. Best skiing was at treeline. One whumph below treeline, non-propogating cracking at treeline. Alpine snowpack (West facing) was thin with lots of sharks! Made it up to the summit of Cryst…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Good ski conditions and fast riding on low angle slopes. Overcast skies and on and off snowing throughout the day. 

Ski depth was going down 10cm but boot depth was to the ground when standing. 

Dug a pit in a moderate slope (20-25 degrees). Column test yielded moderate planar failure at 13 hits, 35cm down at 2173m elevation on a NW Aspect. Repeat on extended column showed no propagation …

reports.title: Puzzle Peak snow profile
reports.comment: quick: 10-20 cm low-density storm snow on the surface made for very good ski quality. No wind effect; fluff, ridge to the valley. The snowpack is weak and we broke through in many places putting in the uptrack. While the ski quality was good on the way down, it was tentative skiing with the shallow, weak snowpack and hidden rocks. The profile showed mid and lower snowpack failures on facets. On th…

reports.title: Bow Falls
reports.comment:
quick: We noticed whumpfing on the approach, most noticeably at the base of the ice, as well as shooting cracks. 

A cornice was present along the top of the cliff band but not directly above the climb.  

Ice conditions- first time climbing, seemed fat and air rated in spots, I would say In good condition.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Started at truck -1 C at 8:45 AM.  Mainly cloudy with no wind.  Dusted of snow in the skin track until across the lake and 1/2 up the approach.  New snow started to become deeper.  Zero instabilities noticed while up tracking.  Occasionally (2-3 x) ski broke through support crust - minor.  Alpine doesn’t have any cornices.  Wind was 0-5 km’s all day.  Temp stayed flat and clouded in / impac…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Snowpack was dry unlike conditions further south.  ECT-M down 40-60 in sudden planar or sudden collapse on facets.  Widespread evidence of cracking, but not extensive propogation.  Upper snowpack is not yet stiff enough for widespread activity.  Surface snow skied well, but sounded and felt a  lot like surface facets. / weather: No snow transport observed early in day, moderate by the end o…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Skied a couple laps of the crowfoot glades area. Pit was dug about 11:15am with both compression test and ECT performed. Compression test yielded two simultaneous failures at 9 taps, fracturing the new/wind loaded snow layer (approx. 10cm down from the surface) and large middle layer overtop large facets that went down to to the ground. ECT failure at 21 taps and full propagation across the…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Skied off Little Crowfoot in light powder and good light. HS 120cm on Ferris glacier, bottom half facets, with thick supportive layer above facets roughly 30-40cm, 10cm light powder on top, estimates from probing, didn’t dig into snow. We avoided thin and steep slopes. Large open holes at top of glacier. Treeline and below was less supportive with surface crust in places.

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot
reports.comment:
snowpack: The first image is the Bow Summit study plot snow profile for January 18, 2023.

The second image is a table showing the past 10 years of total snowpack height (HS) at Bow Summit for mid-January. 

1. Notice how this is the most shallow year in a decade.
2. Years 2019 - 2022 stand out as good years - the past four winters were good ones.
3.  The ten-year average for mid-Jan is 100 cm, we…

reports.title: Watermelon Peak
reports.comment: quick: Had 2 whimpfs on ascent and descent in the alpine,  no shooting cracks. Stayed on slopes 25 degrees or less.  Dug a pit at 2500 m - height if snow was 90 cm, found Jan 4 surface hoar (3-4 mm) down 10 cm with Compression test broken results. Most notable result was the compression test moderate (11 taps) sudden collapse result down 55 cm and repeated twice.  This sun crust on steep solar at …

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up Cirque Forepeak south rib to beneath alpine bench. BTL travel still miserable outside of skin track, but increasingly supportive moving up into TL/Alpine. 

Signs of cross-loading and wind slab in alpine lee features, with poor coverage in windward zones. Low-angle terrain provided turns in light, sugary, snow.
 
Inversion noticed during travel with alpine air temperature at 2500m…

reports.title: Good Travel on Peyto Icefield
reports.comment: quick: Spent 2 nights at the Peyto Hut. Route in from Peyto Lake needs more snow. Skis off in a few places to pass rocky sections with minimal snow cover (particularly thin from the top of the moraines to the weather station). Good firm travel on the glaciers. Skied/climbed Mount Habel one day. We dug a small pit at 2300 meters. 15 cm of storm snow sitting on a solid base. We didn’t see any signs …

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Fantastic day to be out. No signs of whumfing or cracking or instability. A couple of times you would break through the crust layer under the powder to the crap underneath but not triggering happened.

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Toured up to Ferris Glacier via bow hut/crowfoot route. Unsurprisingly, highly variable and wind-affected snowpack moving through moraines. Supportive only where wind/rider compression a factor in gullies. Probed 1.6-2m on glacier @ 2750m.

reports.title: Lake Helen & Katherine Area
reports.comment:
quick: Beautiful day out near Lake Helen. Snow was dust (~10cm) on crust and skied great on mellow lee slopes. Windward slopes were quite bare in the alpine. Snowpack becomes very unsupportive and faceted in the trees, but coverage is improving slowly.
Weather was sunny all day and warmer than expected, felt like spring but with early season snow conditions

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder/Puzzle Peak Ramp
reports.comment: quick: Toured up Dolomite shoulder and puzzle peak ramp. Noticed a sz1 (seemed remote triggered) on east side of shoulder, crown looked about 60cm. HS 105, ct failed on 14 with sudden collapse down 60cm on facets. Stability seems consistent with reports. Good fast pow on low angle terrain with no observed sun or wind effect. Some sharks about.

reports.title: OXO/ Puzzle Peak Ramp
reports.comment:
quick: Great day up the Puzzle Peak Ramp on Sunday. Temps were -10 leaving the car at 9:45 and -6 at the car when we returned around 14:30.  Observed two older sz 1-1.5 wind slabs that had released just below the cornice that is forming on the upper ridge of Dolomite. 

Good, fun snow from about 50m below the top down the ramp, with the ski out in good shape as well. 

Dug a pit @ 2450m on a SW as…

reports.title: Dolomite Traverse
reports.comment: quick: Easy travel coming up Helen Creek. Good turns through soft snow coming down to Katherine Lake. Evidence of wind loading and cracking as you come towards the col behind Dolomite, ski cut two size 1.5 and skied the guts of a very recent size 2 on the Lee side of the col. The luge track out of Dolomite shoulder is very much a choose your own adventure. / avalanche: 1) Saw very recent size 2 na…

reports.title: Oxo/Puzzle Peak Ramp
reports.comment: quick: Great day out. Snow conditions were good on the ramp, heavy powder but we had some great fresh lines. No wumphing or shooting cracks seen. Slight Sun affect on the snow as the day got warmer. We rode slopes less than 30 degrees to minimize risk. Good to see two other groups enjoying the low angle terrain safely.

reports.title: Puzzle Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied puzzle from col beneath unnamed peak. Variable skiing conditions with recent snow (~10cm) barely covering thin, rocky sections on main planar slope. Deeper, supportive snowpack found in gullies adjacent to main slope. 

And surprisingly supportive snow in many places outside skin track BTL, TL, and alpine. Setting a track wasn’t terrible, for once.

reports.title: Puzzle Peak Ramp
reports.comment: quick: Great conditions on the Puzzle Ramp Peak today! There's actually a base starting to form, but it's still possible to sink down in the bottomless facets in spots. Maybe about 10cm of fresh snow, some of which was slabbing up in spots thanks to the wind. We booted up to the summit from the col and there was some thicker reactive wind slab right near the top.  Variable snow conditions up high …

reports.title: Parks Canada Bow Summit plot
reports.comment: snowpack: Not very inspiring in this location!

reports.title: Observation Trees
reports.comment:
quick: Skied 30 deg terrain on supported slopes with minimal wind effect but punchy snow. Avoided any high consequence or convex terrain / weather: Drifting visible in tracks from past 48hrs but no drifting or moving snow during our day. Mostly soft slabs except in immediately wind scoured terrain / snowpack: CT13 SP, down 20 on facets under wind affected snow
CT22 SP, down 47 on Dec 24 facet inte…

reports.title: Bow Summit South- AST2
reports.comment:
snowpack: Multiple compression tests completed in multiple pits, in to locations during an AST2. One ECT produced sudden results, see below:

ECTP12 down 40 on facets sz. 1-2

reports.comment:

Pit Results:

reports.title: Observation Peak Trees
reports.comment: quick: Around 20cm of fist-4 finger HST at Bow Summit in the morning and S1 throughout the day. The midpack is still punchy and variable BTL, becoming mostly supportive to skis at TL and making for nice skiing with the new snow. CTs at TL produced planar results on the storm/facet interface down 20cm, though no propagation on ECTs.

reports.title: 93 N Avalanche Cycle and Bow Summit Treeline Profile
reports.comment: quick: Observed a cycle of size 2-3 avalanches in the alpine and treeline along the 93N between Mosquito Creek and Bow Summit. All aspects and primarily on the west side of the highway. They seemed to be a mixture of storm snow depth and deeper avalanches.

reports.title: Observation Glades Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: This was an attempt to trigger something on this slope that resulted in a much larger event than was expected. The slab initiated after the first skier had skied about 30-40m away from the second skier and propagated past the second skier's feet and up the crest of the ridge above him another 30m. The skier skied sideways along the ridge crest jumping up and down to try to get something…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: incident: The skier that triggered it, skied out of the flank into wind blown rocks (safe spot)

reports.title: Crow Glades
reports.comment: quick: Whumpfing on up track at aprox 2000m, CT 23H sudden collapse/drop @ 55cm ECT no result rutcshblock test failed r5 at 30 cm propagated across Column confidence was low stuck to low angle dense tress well away from over head hazards

reports.title: Avalanches on Jimmy Simpson
reports.comment: quick: Yesterday we saw two wind slab avalanches  approximately size 1.5 on aspect North East North of mount Jimmy Simpson.

reports.title: Avalanches on Jimmy Simpson
reports.comment: quick: Yesterday we saw two wind slab avalanches  approximately size 1.5 on aspect North East North of mount Jimmy Simpson.

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: We rode Jimmy Junior. Conditions were great. 

Compression test at 2150m elevation. Results CTH22 50RP.

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Skied crowfoot glades area. Did a column text at approx 2200m on a north facing slope. Got CTE9 SC down 75cm on the DPL interface, and CTM16 SP down 40cm on the PL interface. We stayed away from wind effected terrain and did not see this problem. Elected to ski the tree triangle and stay out avalanche terrain with 
Any consequence. The snowpack was gaining support but still could be punched…

reports.title: Bow Summit snow profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Full now profile at Bow Summit study plot. Done with our friends the visiting avalanche forecasters from Norway and drafted using the Norwegian snow profile system (RegObs). Interesting to see snow profile data presented in different formats. Unfortunately, the format may be different, but the snowpack is the same - facets from top to bottom with a very weak base and repeated snowpack te…

reports.title: Bow Summit avalanche
reports.comment:
avalanche: Large avalanche above the ski tour lines on Bow Summit that ran down the upper slope and into the gully below (where people sometimes ski). Estimate the avalanche occurred on Wednesday, Feb 22. The avalanche was down to the ground level and the fracture line ranged from 50 cm to 100 cm with lots or rocks.

Of note: the adjacent slope to the north has not avalanched. This slope sometimes…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Found a few good turns on Ferris Glacier and in the trees, but mostly sporadic wind affected snow and crust. Visibility wasn't the greatest, but didn't notice any signs of recent avalanches or instabilities. Didn't probe the glacier, but also didn't see any holes. The creek in the canyon has decent coverage. The walk across the lake at the end of the day is grim, as per usual. The lake itse…

reports.title: Profile, Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: 10 cm overnight and 45 low density cm storm snow over a settled mid-pack which overrides weak basal facets and depth-hoar

reports.title: Crowfoot glade laps
reports.comment: quick: Did a couple of laps of the main north facing slopes of Crowfoot Glades. Lots of tracks but good snow to be found still! No major wind affect in the trees, ski quality remained fairly decent. Dug a quick pit around 2200, north slope. CT hard 26 on the 70cm facets. Good day. Lots of loose dry coming off the wapta, see photo.

reports.title: Oxo/Puzzle
reports.comment: quick: Great day skiing at Oxo today.  Of note there were multiple parties there up to 14 people skiing the slope.  Still room for fresh though.  Ski quality was good in Alp but still some rock sharks to be found.  Boot top powder overlies the previous surfaces mentioned in the bulletin.  No signs of avalanches, no whumphing or cracking except near ridgetop.

reports.title: Dolomite circuit
reports.comment: quick: First of many parties that did the dolomite circuit today. There was a recent track and even off of it wind effect made travel fairly quick and easy. There's an absolute highway in now. We had a significant whumpf on a small unsupported slope today and so continued to avoid slopes of consequence while we enjoying a mostly clear, often sunny, but some times bitterly cold day.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder/Lake Tour
reports.comment: quick: Went up and around Helen Shoulder and out towards Helen Lake before exiting via Helen Creek. Surface snow skied well once warmed by the sun. The exit/creek feels more like late April than early March due to low snow depths. Saw plenty of signs of older avalanches in the area and got to watch a good sized one drop down Crowfoot Glacier. / avalanche: Watched an avalanche come down over the lo…

reports.title: Observed incident on Dolomite Circuity
reports.comment: quick: See incident / avalanche: Our party was not involved in this, nor did we see it first hand. We are just estimating what happened based on the evidence. Since no other MIN report was reported, we decided to do so. / incident: While doing the Dolomite circuit, we noticed this small slab avalanche in the final terrain trap just before hitting the trees. While we didn't observe the actual avala…

reports.title: Wapta traverse in perfect weather
reports.comment: quick: We did the Wapta Traverse from march 4-8 in stellar conditions. Temperature was cold for the whole trip, with alot of sun during the days. We probed around 180cm on the glacier below Gordon. Crevasses are quite filled in (we still roped up for glacier travel), and it is easy to navigate with such good weather. Snow conditions was good with a 15-20cm on certain ski descent. It was starting t…

reports.title: OXO / Puzzle Peak
reports.comment: quick: Soft facets and surface hoar on top of slab layers below, including sun crusts / snowpack: 5-10cm of facets and surface hoar on slab layers. Sun effect at first layer

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Completed Dolomite Circuit. TL and above we experienced significant whumpfs, and spent most of the day with an inclinometer in hand. Observed few older loose dry releases on steep alpine terrain, and numerous slab avalanches most of which appeared to fail on the recent storm layer, some of which stepped down to the DPL, all of which appeared to be from the last few days. Sun was packing a p…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr. Bowl   size 2 remote
reports.comment: quick: Left the car at 0920 -20C climbed into Jimmy Jr. bowl and temps rose as we climbed.  First run from near the base of the cliffs at 1050, second run around 1140.  Recorded air and snow temp around -4C.  Remote triggered a size two slab when our party of two rejoined at the top of the run.  Ran across four of our switchbacks. / avalanche: Start zone was right against the cliffs and was affect…

reports.title: Spicy Conditions/ Sub Observation/ Skier remote 2.0
reports.comment:
quick: We tried to do a mellow circuit up the SE ridge of Sub observation, then down the backside and around to the Cirque / Sub Ops col, but the conditions were too spicy to complete the route. I have done the route numbers times, and even though we
 chose the mellowest route, we still had to turn back. We had numerous settlements low on the SE ridge, and then eventually, skier remoted a size 2 o…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing on the mellower portions of Jimmy Jr. bowl. But clearly very touchy on anything over 30degrees / avalanche: Observed a second party skier remote (or natural?) happened during transition (second lap) with both skiers 10m from start point. Storm snow influenced by strong solar input and rapid temperature rise. At base of bowl top 30cm of snow was -12C and air temp was -8C. At elev…

reports.title: Juancho
reports.comment: quick: We saw avalanches go up to size 1 and a half in the alpine on steep, sunny slopes. This activity started around 11 o clock when the sun warmed the sun up. / weather: The wind was blowing light snow from peaks but not mixing anything up in the treeline/ above treeline. We felt sudden critical warming from -20 temps around 830 to +2 degrees at noon. / snowpack: Saw a sudden failure 120 cm dow…

reports.title: Crowfoot Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Small settlements in wind loaded pockets of inconsequential terrain on approach to Ferris Glacier.  Glacier gear ‘went for a walk’ with us.  Mainly good practice.  Height of terrain and contouring on benches used to mitigate avalanche hazard.  500-750m bootpack to summit on wind blasted ridge.  Main hazard sneaky rocks on descent, need to get skis tuned.  No notables other than a great day

reports.title: Crowfoot Mtn
reports.comment: quick: Blue bird day on Crowfoot Mtn. Were able to ski up all the way to the top, although the last 15 min we were walking pretty gingerly near and on rocks. No avy concern today, but terrain was mellow. Snow was wind affected in some areas, ok elsewhere, and decent on the Ferris glacier. Lots of ski farming on the glacier! Cornices on the ridge were pretty small, canyon is in good shape.

reports.title: South Bow Summit Area
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche ran just south of the southern most runs at Bow Summit. Runout went just beyond the bench below the slope. Didn't observe it happen but saw it on the drive up on the morning of 20 March. Likely happened sometime on March 19.

reports.title: Observation peak
reports.comment: quick: Recent 2.5 deep persistent slab on Observation Peak, with sympathetic 1.5 slab triggered lower down lookers left.

reports.title: Yoho Pk area
reports.comment:
quick: Watched partial cornice fall just N of Bow hut. Saw signs of recent cornice fall on Mt Olive E aspect. 



Near treeline below Bow hut and As of March 19, found snowpack height ~120cm deep with sun crust down 30cm, and large depth hoar at the ground. - All Consistent with what was expected.  

March 22-Near Yoho pk ~4mm surface hoar on the surface, preserved on N aspects. A 2cm thick sun cr…

reports.title: Cirque North Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Pretty good day with amazing views and overall good skiing! We toured up to the base of the South Ridge of Cirque through Helen Creek. The skin track was pretty well frozen and some kick turns in the canyon were slippery to say the least, but it was fast travel, and the snow softened up as we went higher and the day got warmer. There is basically no snow, or really sparse patches of it so w…

reports.title: Observation: still suspect
reports.comment: avalanche: Aware of the previous min, we did a mellow lap in the observation area to lookers right of that slide in slightly less angled terrain. We remote triggered two separate alpine avalanches that ran very slowly and nearly to our tracks. The whole area was pretty miserable skiing with a mix of isothermic snow and hard crust prevalent. We moved across the highway and skied bow summit for the …

reports.title: Mt Patterson
reports.comment: quick: Great day out on Patterson for a summit! It’s a long walk, so thought I’d save someone some trouble. If you’re after good quality skiing, this is not it! Breakable temperature crust. And lots of rocks. But amazing day out! The bootpack is in great shape and we even were able to keep our skis on the way down. Above it there are 2 spots where the creek is filled with debris. No significant si…

reports.title: Flower Windslab Powder
reports.comment: quick: 5cm of Pencil hard breakable windslab in the flower making for challenging skiing. The stem had similar conditions. Moraines and below had dry supportive snow. Several Natural Deep persistent slabs ~48hrs in the surrounding area.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Skied south shoulder gladed area in the Bow Summit Resort.  15cm soft over supportive base.  No failure during ECT and no other signs of instability.

reports.title: Dolomite Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Likely this was in the last 24 hour period. Heli flight from the day before did not observe this avalanche.

reports.title: Grand Daddy
reports.comment: quick: We headed up about 2/3 of Grand Daddy. Approached via the sluff / avy debris in the fan and then booted up. Ski crampons may be helpful. Most of the good snow was stripped from a larger sluff or smaller avy that seemed to initial from a cornice fall that had a crown of about 50-100cm from the terrain to the right of the main couloir.  Pic included. The more north facing tree slopes at the b…

reports.title: Remote Trigger Size 2.5-3 Mosquito Mountain
reports.comment: avalanche: While ascending mosquito mountain on skis, we were sticking to the "safest" terrain. After passing a higher risk spot of 30-35 degree snow on a south slope we gained the ridge, a couple hundred meters later and felt a massive whumpf (very loud and felt it shake underfoot) likely triggered from a thick to thin zone. Regrouping in a safe zone revealed a large remotely triggered avalanche …

reports.title: Mt Gordon - Cold and Windy
reports.comment: quick: Headed for Mt Gordon today. It was quite windy above the Bow Hut with strong winds in your face. The quick travel of last week on the Wapta was not in the cards today. Broke trail both ways as the wind had blown in our tracks on the way back. It never really warmed up and the winds did not abate. We noted a couple of larger sluffs coming out of steep terrain due to the wind transport on Mt …

reports.title: Noseeum chutes
reports.comment:
quick: Stuck to northern aspects as we saw tons of old slides on everything south facing. 
Fairly quick day in Noseeum cut short due to several whumpfing sounds on our way up two of the chutes at the back (east side) of the creek.
Snow was fairly thin everywhere.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Reasonable skiing at Bow Summit. Few people. Stayed off all terrain >25-30deg. Signs of older avalanches in many areas. 5-10cm of snow on crust. Crust at surface <2150, softer above 2150, even in the shade / on polar aspects. Temperature effect on snow evident everywhere below 2200

reports.title: OXO Puzzle Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Got a bit of everything on OXO today, mostly overcast and flurries with strong wind gusts at ridgetop. Alpine skiied surprisingly well, 5cm wind pressed snow over a generally supportive sun crust. Stuck to mellow slopes and were cautious of convex rolls given the snowpack


Dug a quick pit at 2600m, HS 120cm, 5cm fresh snow on top of a series of alternating crust and facet layers that seeme…

reports.title: Fresh avi debris on Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Lots of avalanche debris on Dolomite Circuit today. On approach to Helen Lake two big avalanches have run across the path (old- 1+ ft of fresh snow on top). On the ski-out, passing the big slopes on right on descent from Dolomite pass, everything had slid (see pics). It looked quite recent. First 2/3 of the exposed descent gully was all fresh debris (tough skiing). Last 1/3 of the gully the…

reports.title: Observation Glades
reports.comment: quick: Interesting day at Observation glades. Snow line at ~2000m by 8am. <5cm new snow variably distributed by wind, leaving some aspects stripped to last week's sun crust, and others nicely sifted for enjoyable skiing. After a break in the weather from ~9am-noon, significant snowfall resumed for the duration of the day. Observed several avalanches on the slopes above, all from previous days. Mos…

reports.title: Helen shoulder glades
reports.comment: quick: Good day setting the highway up around the Helen glades area after a foot of snow buried it. Go make use of it kids! There’s enough snow to just barely hit the sun crust underneath so riding quality was pretty good for a S aspect around this time of year. Some drumming noted on the up track. Rode a couple supported steep sections in the glades, no signs of instability there. The new snow wa…

reports.title: Natural avalanche cycle up to size 3 in the 93N area.
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed a natural avalanche cycle up to size 3 on the 93N on Wednesday. Most failed in the previous 24 hrs, but one large avalanche at the south end of Bow Lake occurred while driving by Wednesday morning and was triggered by solar sluffing out of steep rocky terrain. Failure planes appeared to be a mix of recent storm slabs, and step downs to the various deep persistent layers in the …

reports.title: A Little Lost in Little Italy
reports.comment: quick: ‘Skiied’ Dolomite Traverse today. Cloudy with broken periods, S -1 for the majority of the day. Travel below treeline is heinous at best, much to be said for expert alder smashing skills. HS was 40-60 throughout the day, many sharks and thin to thick sections in the area. We attempted to branch out in the alpine, but were met with large settlements and dramatic whumpfs, so we quickly return…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Tried to ski Dolomite shoulder and found terrible conditions. Hard and breakable crust overlaying unsupportive snow. Dug a pit to check out the snowpack and found only 60-65cm of snow total before rock. Column failed in CT 13 on the basal facets. The SE face of the shoulder looks to have slid in the last few days. 

Skiing down was terrible, but got a bit better when the snow softened sligh…

reports.title: Lil Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Went up little crowfoot today and found fairly good ski conditions. Dry snow up high with crusts down low that had a sort of confusing distribution. 
Mainly I wanted to note that the snowpack on the glacier is very thin (to be expected this season) with 100cm to 260cm of coverage, median probed snow depths of 170cm. Limited visibility today but noted a few recent slabs on the west aspect of…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Rode the crowfoot glades. A definite crust on top in places where the sun shines, but in more sheltered areas the snow was pretty good. Lots of evidence of avalanches from the recent cycle.

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the grand daddy couloir this morning. A few old tracks but still skied well! Weather was cloudy with light flurries at times. Winds light. Bow River is still very well bridged. 

Included a few other terrain photos taken today: Hector approach, Andromache approach, Surprise Pass right, Aberdeen N glacier

reports.title: Flower couloir
reports.comment: incident: We made our way to flower couloir and noted some wind loading well below the couloir. As we got closer to the couloir there was minimal wind loading. We started boot packing and for the most part found good supportive snow (10-15 cm of soft on top of firmer snow). We reached a point where the snow changed and became more slab like. At this point we decided to ski down. We cleared the top…

reports.title: St. Nicholas and Mt Olive Col
reports.comment:
quick: The canyon up to Bow hut still has excellent coverage. Convexities in the alpine were touchy, surface wind slab was cracking off the ski. Above Bow Hut the snow on the glacier was good skiing.

At 08:00 we observed an avalanche off the east face of Haddo Peak from the highway, Na, no obvious trigger, large powder cloud suspected size 2 or 3, hard to determine as we could not see the runout.…

reports.title: West Nile Trees
reports.comment: quick: Mellow day checking out conditions - 5-10 cm powder on firm and fairly supportive crust from the road. Decent skiing on descent, generally did not break through the crust. Several smaller wet slides could be seen in the alpine on both sides of the valley. Looked like another party skiied the Grand Daddy today or yesterday.

reports.title: Collie Attempt - Numerous Whumphs
reports.comment: quick: Mostly trying to save someone a long walk here. Attempted Collie today. Made it to the col but did not end up checking out the ridge. We had 21 whumphs leading up to the face in the flatter terrain after leaving the main track that heads to the Guy hut. after we started breaking trail. The whumphs had a weird high pitch sound, more like live rounds whizzing by. We made it to the col and cha…

reports.title: Bow Summit AST 2 Field Day
reports.comment: snowpack: Dug a couple of Snow pits at the top of the bow summit trail during the AST2 course. CT failed at 14 down to deep persistent layer repeatedly. Very firm solid snow layer above the weak facet layer at the bottom. Little to no wind slab evident in the snow pack. Warm weather over Christmas has greatly improved the snow above the deep persistent weak layer. Typical Rocky snow pack, inverted…

reports.title: Warm weather: Bow Canyon / Wapta Icefields
reports.comment: quick: Very warm conditions on the Wapta Icefield but we had overnight freezing April 28 - May 1 with good stability up high. Bow Canyon is melting fast with lots of water. It might be hard to get through after May 1 without cooler temps.

reports.title: Ferris
reports.comment: quick: Gorgeous day out! Decided to check out the Ferris glacier. Approach in actually was reasonable and the canyon skiable however observed numerous small slab releases on some of the canyon exits points failing to ground. ( which could be dangerous if swept in the creek). Further up hard trail breaking through trees and as expected very thin to the glacier. Ferris ranged from 40-80 cm coverage …

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: About 4-5” non breakable crust. CT15 failed at the interface between the melt freeze and the warm wet snow beneath it.

We headed up the north shoulder and left early. The goal was to check if pacmans was doable but the snow hasn’t recovered from the previous heat cycle.
